title: The text discusses the potential role of trade unions, particularly agricultural workers' unions, in enhancing food production and rural development in Africa. It highlights a consultative meeting involving the Pan-African Federation of Agricultural Trade Unions (Pafatu) and the UN Food & Agriculture Organisation, where initiatives to improve rural workers' purchasing power, reduce debt, and provide vocational training were proposed. The text cites successful examples from Ghana's General Agricultural Workers’ Union (Gawu) and mentions the need for unions to expand their reach beyond traditional agricultural sectors. It concludes with a note of caution regarding the effectiveness of these initiatives in delivering real benefits to rural communities.
